summary: Provide ECS mapping + live validation harness for tenant-scoped audit stream
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a canonical Elastic Common Schema (ECS) mapping for Redwood audit events scoped per-tenant, plus a live validation harness that will push sample events to the customer's ECS ingestion endpoint and produce a simple Kibana index template.

Impact: DataStream Analytics is onboarding Redwood audit streams into a consolidated ECS index for SOC/IR workflows. Without a standardized mapping and a validation run they cannot reconcile events with their alerting rules; onboarding is blocked and their SOC integration date is slipping.

Request / Deliverables:
- Author a canonical ECS v1.12 mapping document that maps Redwood audit fields to ECS (e.g., map actor.user_id -> ecs.user.id, request_id -> transaction.id, model_name -> event.dataset or ml.model.name as appropriate).
- Provide a JSON sample mapping (field types/normalization rules) and a Kibana index template example.
- Create a live validation harness (container or simple CLI) that: 1) streams a configurable batch of synthetic tenant-scoped events (default 1000) to the customer's HTTP/HTTPS ECS ingest endpoint, 2) supports both bulk and single-event ingestion modes, 3) signs each batch with an HMAC header per tenant for delivery proof.
- Include normalization rules for timestamps (all to UTC ISO-8601), timezone mapping, and user identifier pseudonymization options (one-way hash vs reversible tokenization).
- Provide an optional small mapping shim customers can run that renames duplicate context.* fields and collapses nested request metadata into ecs.* fields.
- Deliver a short verification report after the run: event counts, example document IDs, any dropped fields, and a checksum manifest for the batch.

Environment / Constraints:
- Target environment: prod cluster (us-east). Customer will provide an HTTPS ingestion endpoint and a client cert if mutual TLS is required.
- Expected ingestion profile for validation: 1k events in burst, up to 5k events/hour sustained for stress test.

Steps to reproduce / test plan (what support/eng should run):
1) Obtain customer's ingest URL and any auth headers/cert.
2) Run the harness locally with --tenant-id <TENANT> --mode bulk --count 1000 against the URL.
3) Observe HTTP 200/201 responses and collect returned document IDs.
4) Verify indexed documents in customer's Kibana using a shared sample query (provided below).

Sample Kibana query (free-text):
- query: event.dataset: (redwood.audit OR redwood.ingest) AND tenant.id: "<TENANT>" | sort @timestamp desc | limit 20

Sample Redwood event (one-line JSON string included as an example payload sent by the harness):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-10T14:23:01Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "request_id": "req_9a8b7c6d",
  "actor": { "user_id": "u-12345", "ip": "52.12.34.56" },
  "action": "model.generate",
  "model": { "name": "gpt-small-2026", "version": "v1.3.0" },
  "prompt_tokens": 86,
  "response_tokens": 412,
  "status": "completed",
  "context": { "session_id": "s-9876", "app_version": "2.14.0" }
}

Logs / evidence customer asked for:
- Example index documents (first 10 samples) produced by the harness.
- Batch checksum manifest (SHA256 per file) and HMAC header proof.
- Minimal Kibana index template JSON.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer can query ECS fields (ecs.user.id, transaction.id, event.dataset, host.geo.* if present) and match counts against Redwood console export for the same tenant/time window.
- Signed batch manifest verifies against delivered file in transit.
- No PII (raw user emails, tokens) are included in the sample data unless explicitly requested and redacted/consented.

Notes: Keep mapping conservative — prefer string typed fields where ambiguity exists (e.g., request_id as keyword). Provide a short mapping appendix that explains why certain fields map to ECS choices (search performance, cardinality concerns).

investigation_notes: Initial mapping draft created: actor.user_id -> ecs.user.id, actor.ip -> client.ip, request_id -> transaction.id, model.name -> ml.model.name, model.version -> ml.model.version.
Observed fields to drop by default: context.debug_trace, internal.* (sensitive operational metadata). Provide an opt-in to keep internal.* for enterprise debugging.
Timestamp normalization: accept both 'timestamp' and '@timestamp' but canonicalize to @timestamp (UTC) in mapping to avoid double-indexing windows.
Rate considerations: Suggest harness supports both bulk API (for Elastic bulk ingest) and HTTP/JSON single events. For sustained verification >2k events/hour prefer bulk + backoff to avoid 429s.
